data.title: The "Share" link: the bill in the page address

events.line: Accepted, I will study the code and write the statement of task 3
events.text:
Write the statement of task 3 from the series for the split-bill project. Tasks 1 and 2 are done and committed, read the code yourself.

Task: the "Share" link. The whole state of the bill is encoded in the page address, without a server; whoever opens the link sees the same bill; a broken or old link does not break the page, but shows a clear message. The mobile layout, the README and deployment to GitHub Pages are the next task and are not part of this one. The site will live in a subdirectory, so the link must work under any base path, for example with the state in the address fragment.

The human's decisions are made in advance: the statement is approved, resolve the forks yourself and put them into the section "Accepted decisions". No new runtime dependencies unless there is a weighty reason. The format must be versioned, so that a link of another version is recognized and gives a clear message, compact (long identifiers in the address are useless, think about reindexing the participants by order), safe for an address and with support for Cyrillic in names. The parsing is strict: types, whole kopecks, references to participants, uniqueness of names, limits. A broken link must neither crash the page nor create an invalid bill.

Encoding and decoding of the bill and the parsing errors as an exhaustive type are the domain part without the DOM, with tests: a round trip, broken strings, an old and a future version, Cyrillic and emoji in names, an empty bill, limits. Reading and writing the address and the clipboard are in the interface.

Decide and write down: whether the address is updated on every change of the bill or only by the button; what the "Share" button does (copies the link and shows "Link copied", and if the clipboard is unavailable, shows the link in a field); what the message about a broken or old link looks like (in plain language, the page works with an empty bill, the message can be closed) and whether an empty bill overwrites a broken address before the first action; whether a reaction to a manual change of the fragment in the same tab is needed. Follow the project rules; name what does not belong to the task in the section "Out of scope".

events.line: Here is the statement: the bill in the address fragment, version 1
events.text:
The statement is ready. Goal: the whole state of the bill is stored in the address fragment without a server. Whoever opened the link sees the same bill, a reload does not lose the bill. A broken link or a link of another version of the format does not break the page, but shows a clear message that can be closed.

Accepted decisions. The state lies in the address fragment, so the link works under any base path, and the path and parameters are kept. The format of the first version: the version number, a dot, the data. The version stands in plain text so that a foreign version can be recognized without parsing the data. The data is JSON from the list of names and the list of expenses, turned into UTF-8 and then into base64url without padding characters. An expense is written as the payer's index, the kopecks and the recipients' indices. The participants are reindexed by order, the identifiers do not get into the link, the order of participants and recipients is kept, because the one who gets the extra kopecks depends on it. After parsing the identifiers are ordinal strings, new ones from the forms still get random ones.

The parsing trusts nothing. The order of checks: the length is at most 100,000 characters; the version is an integer, otherwise "corrupted", not one — "another version"; the alphabet and length of base64url, strict UTF-8, JSON parsing; the structure is exactly a list of names and a list of tuples of three elements; names are non-empty and unique ignoring case; indices are integers and within the list; the amount is a safe integer greater than zero; recipients are non-empty and without repeats. The only limit is the string length, there are no separate limits on the number of participants and expenses. Exceptions from the parsing do not go outside.

The address is updated on every change of the bill, without new history entries, an empty bill is written too. While the user has changed nothing, the address is not touched. A broken or old link: the page works with an empty bill, above the sections a message with a "Close" button is shown, the address is not overwritten until the first change. The texts of the messages: for a corrupted link — that it is corrupted or copied incompletely, for another version — that it was made in another version of "Split the bill"; in both cases one can ask to send the link again or start a new bill. The "Share" button copies the link to the clipboard and shows "Link copied"; if there is no clipboard or the write is rejected, a read-only field with the link and a hint to copy it is shown. A change of the fragment in the same tab is handled the same way as opening: otherwise the person would see the old bill.

Plan: add the DOM ban for the new directory to the linter config; add a check of the list of names in linear time; write the base64url encoding and the bill code module with the error and result types; move working with the address into one interface module; make the message plate about the link and the "Share" section the last one on the page; in the app write the code on every change and open the bill from the address on start and on a change of the fragment; add minimal styles.

Done criteria: make check is green; the linter fails on access to the DOM from the new directory; round-trip encoding keeps the bill up to the identifiers; broken strings give errors of the right kind; after a change of the bill the address contains its code, the history does not grow; a new app at the same address shows the same bill; a broken fragment gives a message and an empty bill without changing the address; "Share" copies the link keeping the path or shows the field; a change of the fragment opens another bill or the message. The tests lie next to the code and cover the encoding, round-trip cases with Cyrillic and emoji, all kinds of broken strings, versions and interface scenarios with a substituted clipboard.

Out of scope: the mobile layout, the README, Pages, compression, compatibility with past versions of the format. Noticed on the way and not fixed: the total of the expenses can exceed a safe integer, and the forms have no limits on the name length and the number of participants and expenses. The decisions should be written into the project journal, like the previous ones.

events.line: Accepted. I make the link: encoding, parsing, address, button
events.text:
Do task 3 of the split-bill project by the approved statement. Tasks 1 and 2 are committed. Do not commit — the lead will do it. First read the project rules: names from the domain, no magic values, immutability of the input, one function — one action, nesting no deeper than two, an intermediate result gets a name, a flag does not switch behavior, errors are not swallowed, texts and comments in Russian, identifiers in English.

The lead's correction: the text for a link of another version is this — "This link was made in a different version of the app, and it can't be opened here. Ask for a new link, and meanwhile you can start a new bill."

The content of the statement: the bill state lies in the address fragment in the format of the first version — the version number, a dot and base64url of JSON of names and expenses in UTF-8; the participants are reindexed, the identifiers after parsing are ordinal. The parsing trusts nothing and checks in order the length, version, alphabet and UTF-8, JSON, structure, names, indices, amounts and recipients; there are three kinds of errors — corrupted, another version, invalid bill. The address is updated on every change of the bill without new history entries and is not touched until the first change. A broken or old link gives an empty bill and a closable message. The "Share" button copies the link and writes "Link copied", and without a clipboard shows a field with the link. A change of the fragment is handled the same way as opening.

By the plan: extend the DOM ban to the new directory in the linter; add a check of the list of names; write the modules of base64url encoding and the bill code without the DOM; move working with the address into one module; make the message plate and the "Share" section the last one on the page; connect writing and reading the address in the app; add styles. The done criteria and the list of tests are given in the statement. When remounting in tests, the fragment-change handlers of past apps stay on the window, so make the tests not interfere with each other in the simplest and honest way, for example by returning an unsubscribe function.

Out of scope: the mobile layout, the README, Pages, compression, compatibility with old versions of the format, a limit on the sum of all expenses and on the name length in the forms.

At the end run the formatting and make check, it must be green. In the answer write what was done by the points of the plan, what deviations there were and why, and the result of the checks.

events.line: Here you are. Task 3 is ready, make check is green, 248 tests
events.text:
Task 3 is done. Formatting and then make check are green: types, linter, 248 tests in ten files and the build. Nothing is committed. The linter criterion was checked by hand: a temporary file in the new directory with accesses to location, navigator, window and an import of the interface gives four errors; the file is removed.

By the points of the plan. In the linter config the new directory is added to the DOM ban, the rule texts became neutral. In the bill logic a check of the list of names in one pass is added. The base64url encoding is done by the plan, exceptions turn into an empty result; bytes are turned into a string without spread, so as not to fail on large inputs, and there is a test on 300,000 characters for this. The bill code module contains the version, the length limit, the error types, the encoding and the parsing with the checks in the needed order; the parsing goes in steps, each check in its own function. The tests cover all cases from the statement and check only the kind of the error. The address module is the only place where location and history are used. The message plate uses an exhaustive switch and the texts from the statement, including the lead's correction. The "Share" section copies the link and, when the clipboard is missing or refuses, shows a read-only field. In the app the order is: the header, the message, four sections; a change of the bill writes the address, opening from the address is called at start and on a change of the fragment. Styles are added. In the app tests the start function now returns an unsubscribe, the tests call it on remounting too; the new block covers the address, the history, the path, remounting, broken links, closing the message, a change of the fragment and three states of the clipboard.

Deviations and remarks. The start returns an unsubscribe function. Added is the rule that hidden elements are really hidden: without it the flex styles would override the hidden attribute, and the message and the fallback field would always be visible; it also fixes the earlier expense form. Numbers in templates are wrapped in String because of a linter rule. The message "Link copied" is red because it is shown in the area of errors; it is better to fix it in task 4. Version 01 passes as version 1, the app cannot encode it that way. A race: if the bill changes before the clipboard answers, the late answer will write "Link copied" over the reset message; I did not fix it, out of scope.

events.line: Accepted. I will check the criteria and try to break the parsing
events.text:
Review the uncommitted changes for task 3. Tasks 1 and 2 were committed earlier, review only task 3. Experiments that break the code do in a copy in a temporary directory. Do not change files.

Task: the "Share" link. The whole state of the bill is encoded in the page address without a server, the link opens the same bill, and a broken or old link does not break the page and shows a clear message.

The key decisions of the statement: the state in the address fragment; the format of the first version — the version number, a dot, base64url of JSON of names and expenses; the identifiers do not get into the link; after parsing they are ordinal; the parsing trusts nothing and checks the length, version, alphabet, UTF-8, JSON, structure, names, indices, amounts and recipients; the address is updated on every change of the bill and is not touched until the first change; a broken or old link gives an empty bill and a closable message with the given texts; "Share" copies the link or shows a read-only field; a change of the fragment is handled the same way as opening. The domain part lies in a separate directory without the DOM, the address — only in the address module.

Done criteria: make check is green; the linter fails on access to DOM globals and on an import of the interface from the new directory; for any bill from the interface the encoding and parsing return the same bill up to the identifiers; broken strings give errors of the right kind, exceptions do not fly out of the parsing; after a change of the bill the address contains its code, the history does not grow; a new app at the same address shows the same bill; a broken fragment gives a message and an empty bill without changing the address until the first change; "Share" calls the clipboard write and shows "Link copied", the path is kept, without a clipboard or on a refusal the field is visible; a change of the fragment opens another bill or the message.

Assess the executor's deviations and reservations and say for each whether it is justified and whether it needs fixing in this task: the start function returns an unsubscribe; the rule that hidden elements are hidden; wrapping numbers in String; the red color of the message "Link copied"; version 01 passes as 1; the race with the clipboard.

Check especially that the parsing can neither crash the page nor create an invalid bill: try strange inputs in the copy — a prototype service name, nested arrays, huge arrays within the length, long strings after the version, percent-encoding of the fragment. Check the project rules: readability, nesting up to two, names, errors are not swallowed, especially in the catch blocks around decoding and JSON parsing, immutability. Check whether there are secret leaks.

events.line: Returning it: a forged link crashes the page, there are seven more
events.text:
SENT BACK FOR REWORK. Checked: make check in the copy is green (248 tests, types, linter, build). I ran strange inputs: a prototype service name, nested arrays, nesting 37,000 deep within the length, 6000 expenses, unusual version notations, percent-encoding, a sparse array and empty values among the recipients. No input threw an exception from the parsing. I did not touch the working copy.

Serious. First: a forged link crashes the page. Each amount is checked for a safe integer, but the bill total is not. There are links where the amounts are acceptable separately, but precision is lost when they are added, and the transfer calculation throws an exception about a non-zero sum of balances. I found such a link by search: the app crashes on it, the summary is not rendered, the fragment-change handler is not attached because the exception flies out earlier. This breaks the main requirement of the task. It can be fixed like this: when assembling the bill, reject it as invalid if the total of the expenses is not a safe integer, and add a test for such a pair of amounts. The same hole existed before this task, the expense form accepts several amounts of 90 trillion rubles; this is out of scope of task 3, but it must be named in the report.

Medium. Second: the DOM ban for the new directory is incomplete. ESLint lets through history, globalThis.location, self.location, sessionStorage, fetch and HTMLElement, and the main hole is history, which writes the address. At least history, self, globalThis and sessionStorage must be added. Third: the race in "Share" is worse than the executor described. Besides a late success, a late refusal is possible, and then the field will show the link of an outdated bill. It can be fixed now by remembering the state at the moment of the click, or explicitly postponed with a note in the report. Fourth: a bill from the interface does not always survive the reverse encoding. A name of 40,000 characters gives a code longer than the limit, the parsing will return "corrupted", and the address is still written; after a reload the person will lose the data. Either limit the name length and the number of expenses in the interface or explicitly write down a reservation. Fifth: "Link copied" is shown in the red error color. Moving it to task 4 is justified only if it is about the design of messages, otherwise it is simpler to add a class modifier now.

Small. Sixth: the names data and parseData are forbidden by the project rules, payload and parsePayload will do. Seventh: the condition of the clipboard being present should be named, for example isClipboardAvailable. Eighth: a multiline if without braces, it must be uniformly with braces.

Assessment of the executor's deviations. The unsubscribe function is justified. The rule about hidden elements is justified, though fragile. Wrapping numbers in String is justified. The red message — see the fifth. Version 01 is harmless. The race — see the third, the refusal is worse.

On strange inputs the parsing behaves well: a percent-encoded fragment gives "corrupted" and a clear message, a prototype service name is harmless, the catch blocks do not swallow errors but turn them into a result with a reason, the inputs are not changed, there are no secrets. Except for the second and the fourth, criteria 1–9 are covered by tests.

events.line: Understood, fixing: the total sum, the DOM ban, the race, the name, the color
events.text:
Rework task 3 of the split-bill project after the review (the first return). The changes lie uncommitted in the working copy, this is your previous attempt, continue from it. Read the project rules, do not commit. At the end run the formatting and make check, it must be green.

The task and the criteria are the same: the bill in the page address without a server, a broken or old link does not break the page, but shows a clear message. Do not break the other criteria and the existing tests.

The review remarks and the lead's decisions.

First, serious: a forged link crashes the page. The amounts are safe integers separately, but the total loses precision when added, and the transfer calculation throws an exception before the fragment-change handler is attached. The lead's decision: the rule "the sum of all expenses is a safe integer" lives in one place in the bill logic, for example a separate check based on the total of the expenses, the limit is a named constant equal to the maximum safe integer, with a comment on why: with a larger sum the balances lose precision. The rule is used in two places. The link parsing rejects such a bill as invalid, with tests for the pair of amounts from the example and for the example itself: the page shows the message about a corrupted link, does not crash, the fragment change works. The expense form does not add an expense after which the total would exceed the limit and shows a short clear message about too large an amount, with a test. This closes the same hole in the form that existed before the task.

Second, medium: the ban on DOM globals for the bill logic, the calculations and the new directory is incomplete. Add history, self, globalThis, sessionStorage and fetch. Make sure the code in these directories does not use globalThis legitimately, and check in a copy that the linter fails on each of them.

Third, medium: the race in "Share". A late clipboard answer after a change of the bill writes "Link copied" over the reset message, and a late refusal shows the field with an outdated link. Fix it now: an answer that came after the redraw of the section is ignored. A test: press "Share", change the bill before the answer, then resolve or reject the promise — neither the message nor the field appears.

Fourth, medium: a name of 40,000 characters gives a code longer than the limit, after a reload the link is considered corrupted and the data is lost. The lead's decision: limit the participant name length with the constant 40, add the name problem variant "too long" to both name checks, the length is counted after trim in the characters that a person sees; the text in the form is "Name is longer than 40 characters — shorten it" with the number from the constant; the link parsing applies the same rule as an invalid bill. The remaining theoretical limit, when hundreds of participants or thousands of expenses give a code longer than the limit, is a deliberate limitation: describe it in one phrase in the comment at the code length limit constant. Tests: in the bill logic, in the parsing (a name of 41 characters is an error; 40 characters of Cyrillic and emoji — a round trip) and the form message.

Fifth, medium: "Link copied" is red. Fix it now: the success message gets its own neutral or green style, the errors stay red.

Sixth, small: rename data and parseData to payload, encodedPayload and parsePayload. Seventh: name the condition of the clipboard being present isClipboardAvailable. Eighth: make the multiline if with braces.

In the answer write what changed for each remark, disagreements with the reason and the result of the checks.

events.line: Here you are. All 8 remarks are fixed, 267 tests green
events.text:
All 8 remarks are fixed without disagreements. Formatting and make check are green: types, linter, tests (267, before the rework there were 248) and the build. Nothing is committed.

First, the forged link. In the bill logic a limit constant for the sum is added, equal to the maximum safe integer, with a comment on "why", and a check based on the total of the expenses; the rule lives only here. The link parsing rejects a bill that exceeds it as invalid. The expense form does not add an expense after which the total would exceed the limit and shows a message about too large an amount; the bill and the address do not change. Tests: a total exactly at the limit passes, above it is rejected, the three amounts from the example are rejected, the example link from the review shows the message about a corrupted link, the bill is empty, the fragment change after it works; a separate test for the form.

Second, the DOM ban. History, sessionStorage, fetch, self and globalThis are added to the list of banned globals. There is no legitimate use of globalThis in these directories. In a temporary file the linter fails on all ten globals and on the import of the interface; the file is removed.

Third, the race. In the "Share" section the redraw counter grows on every redraw, a clipboard answer after a redraw is ignored. Two tests with a controllable promise, for resolving and for refusal after a change of the bill; without the check of the outdated answer both fail.

Fourth, the name length. Added are the limit of 40 characters, the variant "too long" and the check in both name checks after trimming spaces, in code points. String spread is forbidden by the linter, so Array.from is used; code points are chosen so that a chain of combining characters does not bypass the limit. The link parsing considers such a name an invalid bill. Next to the code length limit there is one phrase about the deliberate limitation concerning hundreds of participants and thousands of expenses. In the form the text "Name is longer than 40 characters — shorten it" takes the number from the constant. I did not set the maxLength attribute on the field: it counts UTF-16 units and would cut 40 emoji to 20. Tests: the bill logic, the parsing (41 characters — an error, 40 characters of Cyrillic and emoji — a round trip), the form message.

Fifth, the color. A green success style is added, the class is set on success and removed on redraw; the errors stay red. There is a test.

Sixth, seventh and eighth. data and parseData are renamed to payload, encodedPayload and parsePayload, the word "data" in comments and messages is replaced by "payload" (in Russian). The condition of the clipboard being present is named isClipboardAvailable. The multiline if got braces.

For the report. A deliberate limitation remains: a bill with hundreds of participants or thousands of expenses gives a code longer than the limit and after a reload opens as a corrupted link; it is described in the comment at the constant. Version 01 still passes as version 1, as agreed.

events.line: Accepted: all remarks are fixed, four small things remain
events.text:
ACCEPTED. make check is green: types, linter, 267 tests, build. In the copy I separately checked the linter: a file in the new directory with accesses to location, window, navigator, history, sessionStorage, fetch, self, globalThis, document, localStorage and with an import of the interface gives 11 errors, one per each violation.

All remarks of the previous round are fixed. A forged link no longer crashes the page: the check of the limit sum is applied in the parsing, where it gives an invalid bill, and in the expense form, where the expense is not added and the address does not change. A false "within the limit" under rounding does not happen, because the amounts are positive and the partial sums grow. The ban on DOM globals is extended and works. The race in "Share" is closed with a redraw counter, there are tests for a late success and a late refusal. The name length rule is the same in the form and in both name checks, there are tests, including a round trip on Cyrillic and emoji; the code length limitation is described in a comment. A green success style is added, there is a test. There is no data in identifiers any more, the word "payload" (in the Russian comments) reads normally on the whole, except for one place. The condition of the clipboard being present is named, the if has braces. Criteria 1–9 are met, criterion 3 — with a reservation about the code length limit, which the lead accepted.

Small things, they do not interfere with the criteria. First: the function that shows the field with the link does not remove the success class. If after a successful copy "Share" is pressed again without a change of the bill and the clipboard refuses, the text asking to copy the link from the field will look green; I confirmed this with a trial test and suggest removing the class and adding a test. Second: after the word was replaced in the comment of the code module, gender and number no longer agree in the Russian text, the relative pronoun has to be in the feminine form ("the format of which"). Third: the comment at the name length limit promises the characters that a person sees, but the check counts code points; the comment must be fixed. Fourth: several test names still say "data", while the code already says "payload".

There are no other logic errors or rule violations in the new fixes: nesting is no deeper than two, conditions have names, errors are not swallowed, an outdated clipboard answer is dropped intentionally and this is explained in a comment, the input data is not changed, there are no magic values. There are no secrets or server addresses in the changes.

events.line: Accepted. I will make four small fixes before the checks
events.text:
Make four small fixes in the uncommitted task 3 of the split-bill project (the "Share" link, the bill state in the address). The review accepted the task, these are small things before the checks. Read the project rules, do not commit and change nothing beyond the listed.

First: the function that shows the field with the link does not remove the success class. The scenario: "Share", a success with the green "Link copied", "Share" once more without a change of the bill, the clipboard refused, and "Copy the link from the field" is shown in green. Remove the success class in this function and add a test for this scenario.

Second: in the comment of the bill code module the phrase "not parsing the payload, whose format we do not know" (in Russian) does not agree in gender and number. Rewrite it correctly, for example "whose format we do not know" with the feminine pronoun. At the same time reread the other Russian comments and messages in this file where "data" was mechanically replaced by "payload", and fix the agreement.

Third: the comment at the constant of the maximum name length promises "characters that a person sees", but the check counts Unicode code points, for example "👩‍👩‍👧" is 5. Fix the comment: the length is in code points, and why — the limit in the link is hard, composite characters do not bypass it.

Fourth: in the names of the parsing tests there remain "no data after the dot", "foreign characters in the data" and "extra dot in the data". Bring them to one term with the code and the neighboring tests — "payload".

At the end run the formatting and make check, it must be green. In the answer write what changed and the result of the checks.

events.line: Done. Four small things are made, make check is green
events.text:
All four fixes are made. Formatting is done, make check is green: linter, 268 tests in ten files and the build. Nothing is committed.

First: the function that shows the field with the link now removes the success class before showing "Copy the link from the field". A test is added to the app tests: the first copy passes, the second is rejected, the bill does not change between them; the test checks the text and the absence of the success class. I did not separately check that the test fails without the fix.

Second: in the bill code module the phrase is corrected to "whose format" (the feminine pronoun, in Russian). I reread the other Russian comments and messages in the file, gender and number agree there, no other fixes were needed.

Third: the comment at the name length limit now says that the length is counted in Unicode code points, not in the characters that a person sees; the reason is that the link size is strictly limited, and composite characters must not bypass it. The example in the comment: "👩‍👩‍👧" is 5 code points.

Fourth: the names of the parsing tests are renamed to "no payload after the dot", "foreign characters in the payload" and "extra dot in the payload" (in Russian).

events.text:
CHECKS PASSED. I found no defects. I changed only one test file of the bill code module, I did not touch the code.

make check is green after formatting: types, linter, 270 tests in ten files and the build. The linter for the new directory was checked in a copy: accesses to location, window, navigator, history, globalThis, self, sessionStorage, fetch and document give the globals ban error, an import of the interface gives the import ban error.

The round-trip encoding is covered: there were already tests on an empty bill, names with special characters and emoji, a name of 40 code points, the maximum safe sum, the order of recipients and the code pattern. I added a check on 300 pseudo-random bills with a generator with a fixed seed: Cyrillic, emoji and special characters in names up to 40 code points, up to 8 participants and up to 10 expenses, random subsets and order of recipients; the bill equals the original up to the identifiers, the code matches the pattern. The parsing errors are covered by the existing tests: corrupted, invalid bill (including the amount 1e400) and another version with a number. I added a mutation test: in 300 valid codes one character is deleted or replaced, the parsing throws no exceptions and returns either an error or a bill acceptable by the project rules. A forged link with a huge total is covered by an app test.

The address and history, remounting, a broken and an old fragment, "Share" with the clipboard, without it and on a refusal, a late clipboard answer, keeping the path and a change of the fragment are covered by app tests. In the browser I ran Chromium through the build, the preview and Playwright: after adding a participant the history length did not grow, after a reload the page text matched, the link in a new tab showed the same bill, a garbage fragment showed the message about a corrupted link, a fragment of another version — the message about the version, there are no page errors, after a click the clipboard contains the link and "Link copied" appeared. The first run of the tab comparison gave a false result because of an error in the text comparison itself, the repeated one matched.

Only this remained unchecked: a path with a subdirectory was not checked in the browser, the preview worked at the root, but this case is covered by an app test.
